hero.name: Dr Yang Bong
hero.role: Senior Lecturer, School of Business and Law
hero.bio: My research is multidisciplinary, sitting where digital technologies, participatory research and business meet. It spans digital inclusion, rural and Indigenous entrepreneurship, subsistence marketplaces, platform economies and AI for sustainable development, combining community co-design with machine learning and data analytics.

about.heading: About
paragraphs: I am a Senior Lecturer in the School of Business and Law at Birmingham Newman University. My PhD in Digital Economy is from the University of Nottingham, completed with the Horizon Centre for Doctoral Training.

Alongside community-engaged fieldwork with rural and Indigenous micro-entrepreneurs, I also employ machine learning and data analytics to study platform economies. The [Asia-Europe for AI (AE4AI) Network](https://www.asiaeurope4ai.org/), which I helped found, is another strand of this work: I coordinate the network and its AI for Sustainable Development working group. My career began in industry, with eight years in international marketing and business development.

research.heading: Research
research.intro: Current work follows three connected themes.

themes.title: Digital inclusion and subsistence marketplaces
themes.description: AI and digital inclusion with underserved communities, digital appropriation in subsistence marketplaces, and digital entrepreneurship ecosystems.

themes.title: Machine learning for social science
themes.description: Machine learning and data analytics for social-science research, including innovation in agriculture research and household energy.

themes.title: AI for sustainable development
themes.description: The role of universities and local institutions in socially grounded innovation.

items.title: Horizon CDT impact project
items.text: This Horizon CDT impact project, which I secured and delivered, co-designed digital marketing and market-access activities with rural and Indigenous micro-entrepreneurs in Malaysia. Working with the Lun Bawang community of Long Semadoh in rural Lawas, Sarawak, and with the creative agency The Culture Capital, the project grew from digital marketing training into a village-wide branding campaign shaped by community leaders and entrepreneurs.

items.text: First author of the White Paper for Universities on Navigating Artificial Intelligence Innovation Ecosystems in AI for Sustainable Development, produced through the 6th ASEF Higher Education Innovation Laboratory.

project.heading: Long Semadoh, Sarawak
project.summary: In the Lun Bawang highlands of Lawas, the project brought together village leaders, local micro-entrepreneurs and The Culture Capital to co-design a village-wide brand, so that the community could tell its own story to visitors and buyers.
project.quoteNote: The campaign’s tagline invites visitors who truly want to come, while keeping numbers manageable for the village.
outputs: Instagram and Facebook accounts designed for the community to run
Product packaging with a QR code linking to those accounts
Videos, photographs and community interviews for future marketing
A branding and digital marketing workshop for ten micro-entrepreneurs, taught in Malay
